messages.author: 6f9ed2e901fd5760
messages.subject: R newbie need help with SEM models. Help need urgently!!
parts:
I'm using the lavaan package to run SEM.

My supervisor told me to use the following methods as an example of how to run them:

1. extract the factor scores from the fitted models. To do that you need to use the "predict" command. 

e.g. 

engagement_factors <- predict(fit1)

futurebias_factors <- predict(fit2)


2. combine all variables to a new dataset: 

e.g.

newdata <- data.frame(engage1 = engagement_factor$factor1, engage2 = engagement_factor$factor2, fb1 = futurebias_factors$factor1, fb2 = future_bias_factors$factor2)


3. define your sem model 


sem_model1 <- " 

engage1 ~ fb1 + fb2 

engage2 ~ fb1 + fb2 " 


4. Run your sem model 


sem_fit <- sem (sem_model, data = newdata)

summary (sem_fit, standardized =TRUE)


When I ran the first part (1) it does not return factor scores. Instead, it gives me means, medians and quartiles etc. 


orientations_factors <- predict(fit)


automousmotivation_factors <- predict(fit2)


engagement_factors <- predict(fit3)

#Meaningfulness not possible due to only 2 items

Meaningfulness_factors < predict(Meaningfulness)


psychologicalmeaningfulness_factors <- predict(fit4)


jobchallenge_factors <- predict(fit5)


futurebias_factors <- predict(fit6)


selfregulation_factors <- predict(Fit7)


egodepletion_factors <- predict(fit8)


Any ideas on where I am going wrong?


I would also appreciate guidance on defining my sem model and running it.

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: R newbie need help with SEM models. Help need urgently!!
parts:
Hi

You are making a multiple step process when you should do the SEM model in 1 model, without extracting factor scores. 

First model: CFA, measuremnte model of your factors of interest, for example something like this. From this model you want to stablish that items are proper to define the latent constructs

mod1 <- '
engage1 =~ item1 + item2 +item3
engage2 =~ item4 + item5 +item6
fb1 =~ item7 + item8 +item9
fb2 =~ item10 + item11 +item12
'

Then, second model, your latent regression model, this model estimates the regressions between latent factors, as latent factors, instead of using factor scores

mod2 <- '
engage1 =~ item1 + item2 +item3
engage2 =~ item4 + item5 +item6
fb1 =~ item7 + item8 +item9
fb2 =~ item10 + item11 +item12

engage1 ~ fb1 + fb2 

engage2 ~ fb1 + fb2
